## Example 6.14 · Part (a) {#iv6-example-6-14-a .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson .a-wide}

```{=html}
<p>Consider the points <span data-math="A(1,-1,3)"></span>, <span data-math="B(2,-4,5)"></span> and <span data-math="C(5,-13,11)"></span>.</p><p>a) Show by calculation that the points <span data-math="A"></span>, <span data-math="B"></span>, <span data-math="C"></span> are collinear</p><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show solution</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="AB=\sqrt{(2-1)^2+(-4+1)^2+(5-3)^2}=\sqrt{14}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="BC=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(-13+4)^2+(11-5)^2}=\sqrt{126}=3\sqrt{14}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="AC=\sqrt{(5-1)^2+(-13+1)^2+(11-3)^2}=\sqrt{224}=4\sqrt{14}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="AB+BC=\sqrt{14}+3\sqrt{14}=4\sqrt{14}=AC"></span></div><p>The lengths add exactly, so <span data-math="B"></span> lies on the line segment <span data-math="AC"></span>. Hence the points are collinear.</p></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 51</div>

::: notes
Additional application. Use the distance formula for (a), giving a calculation distinct from the vector argument in (b). Equality of path length AB+BC with direct distance AC means the three distinct points lie on one straight line with B between A and C.
:::
